answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashing bond before it may submit work, then score contributions through randomly assigned peers whose own bonds are at risk for approving fraud. A hollow account cannot create influence merely by multiplying names: each new identity needs fresh capital, while colluding reviewers risk losing theirs. The ember of a small initial stake may be enough to enter, but scaling a Sybil cluster ties up far more funds, and detected abuse burns the bond. A rate-limited inlet can further prevent one funded identity from flooding review queues.
